actual_checks: Full prompt, wrapper/meta, source/report/provenance and full earlier contribution read. Conditional categorization is essential and preserved: the all-convex-C1,1 total-curvature hypothesis is additional. The source reduction, exact profile mechanism, singularity issues and rigidity provide substantial content beyond the earlier normalization observation/announcement.

With ambient dimension m=n+1>=2, unit-ball volume omega_m and sphere area m*omega_m, the sharp coefficient is m^(-m/(m-1))*omega_m^(-1/(m-1)); the literal (m-1) coefficient is strictly larger. For positive-volume regular open regions the resulting literal inequality is strict. Empty/zero-volume cases do not support that strictness claim.

The hypothesis ranges over every closed convex C1,1 hypersurface in the fixed complete simply-connected nonpositively curved manifold. Source Lemma 7.2 separates singularities from the convex-hull contact region and gives obstacle C1,1 regularity. Proposition 6.6 transfers total curvature to that contact portion; a generic nonconvex boundary cannot replace it.

Checked normalized mean curvature, determinant <=H^(m-1), m*omega_m<=H0^(m-1)*I_B, first variation I_B-prime=(m-1)*H0 and derivative of I_B^(m/(m-1)) >=m*(m*omega_m)^(1/(m-1)). Integrating with the credited profile regularity yields the sharp constant. Bounded finite-perimeter sets are covered by the source; regular boundary measure agrees with perimeter. Euclidean-ball rigidity concerns the sharp inequality, not the larger printed coefficient.
